newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV strikes oil, gas north of Vienna.
newsitem.headline: OMV strikes oil, gas north of Vienna.

text.p: Austrian oil and chemicals group OMV said on Tuesday it had located promising oil reserves and made two gas finds in exploratory drilling in the Vienna basin north of the capital.
OMV said two further exploration drills were planned for this year, and six for next. "We expect to make more new finds," the company said in a statement.
"By exploiting these new oil and gas reserves we will be able to maintain our production and supply Austria with domestic oil and gas," it continued.
Austrian oil reserves have become depeleted in recent years but now OMV is pinning its hopes on new technology.
The company was unavailable for comment on the size of the discovered reserves or the quality of the oil found.
OMV said it discovered gas at a depth of 1,000 metres in the Spannberg South 1 drill. A sandstone bank 30 metres thick was found to be entirely filled with gas.
Ebenthal 6 Drill hit upon a 12-metre thick sandstone layer at a depth of 1,700 metres, again filled with gas.
At the third site, Bernhardsthal Sued 3, near the Czech border, oil was discovered in a 10-metre thick sandstone layer 1,700 metres underground.
